question: Audited financial statements as the only bequest measure: read the FY2024 audited statements of the top-20 sponsors (sponsor websites, robots permitting) and record any separately disclosed bequest, estate, planned-gift, split-interest or beneficial-interest-in-trust revenue or asset line, with its amount and share of contributions
conclusion_affected: Whether bequest and estate inflows into DAFs can be sized at all from public data
rationale: Form 990 has no bequest line (Part VIII, Schedule D Part I and Schedule M all lack one) and Schedule B names are not public. Across 20 returns only $1,567,325 of life insurance is itemised. Audit notes are the remaining public place a split could appear

question: Fill the five unknown defaults at death: AEF (program description or DAF application), Greater Horizons and Dechomai (fund agreements), GS DAF and Raymond James Charitable (current circulars from a robots-allowed host, or owner reads manually), and re-read the DAFgiving360 and NCF terms by hand (both hosts are blocked for scripts)
conclusion_affected: Count of sponsors defaulting to their own general fund (11 of 15 known)
rationale: Of 20 sponsors, 5 defaults are unknown (3 not found, 2 robots-blocked), and 2 more rest on repo carry-overs from blocked hosts

question: Generation caps beyond the top 20: code successor-generation limits and default dispositions for the next 30 community-foundation and faith sponsors by DAF assets, to test whether caps (SVCF 3 successors, CCT two generations, FFTC one generation unless authorised, CJP children by default) are a community-foundation pattern
conclusion_affected: Claim that hard caps occur only at community and federation sponsors while nationals state perpetuity
rationale: All four caps or one-generation defaults in the top 20 are community or federation sponsors; NPT, Vanguard and JCF state perpetual succession; the sample is 15 sponsors with a generation row

question: Legacy-flow disclosure: ask whether any sponsor or DAFRC publishes counts or dollars of DAF accounts that transferred to successors, to named charities, or to the sponsor's general fund at the donor's death (search giving reports, DAFRC releases, and community-foundation annual reports for 'successor', 'legacy plan', 'Endowed Giving Program')
conclusion_affected: Whether outflows at death to sponsor pools are material; size of sponsor general funds fed by orphaned DAFs
rationale: No figure found in Fidelity's 2025/2026 Giving Reports and impact snapshot, NPT's 2025 Annual Report, Vanguard's 2025 annual-report page or SVCF's annual-report page

question: Sponsor general-fund inflows from terminated DAFs: for sponsors whose default is a named internal fund (NPT Giving Fund, Vanguard Philanthropic Impact Fund, BofA CGF General Fund, JCF Special Gifts Fund, MS GIFT Undesignated Fund), find any public report of that fund's annual receipts or grants and test whether they track DAF terminations
conclusion_affected: Size of sponsor-controlled grantmaking created by default dispositions
rationale: 11 of the 15 known defaults send un-planned balances to a sponsor-controlled pool; the 990 shows these only as internal transfers, if at all
